_note: M7 travel (P6, T11): the flute's song, the waystones, the paid traveller. crates/core/src/travel.rs reads this file, compiled in: these are rules, not presentation. Notes are the flute's five keys (the arrows and Space, Ocarina of Time's four C buttons and A); the staff draws them from the bottom up in 'staff' order. Each point names its place in data/places.json, where its waystone stands. Prices are coins: base plus a coin for every per_m metres from the traveller to the waystone, held to most. Ticks are 1/60 s.
_song: the travel song: six notes, taught by the trainer with the flute
_strafing: T35 (phase G2): the song of strafing, written in the lid of the hub's side chest (CW-Q27's seven notes, as the journal drew them). Played, for ticks (60 s) the drawn sword's steps to the side go strafe_pct faster (2.2 to 3.5 m/s); the run, the sprint and steps ahead or back are as they were (the person: 'speed up your strafing in combat, not your sprint')
_points: each point's waystone stands in its place in data/places.json; one 'on' the crown stands up the great tree before the boss's door (data/dungeon.json's climb.waystone, T34), its place naming only its map mark. The traveller rides only to waystones on the ground. Then the town's market and the great well (the person: 'the town should have a waystone, and there should be a waystone at the great well'), after the six so a save's woken list reads as it did
_reach_m: coming this near a waystone counts as having been there: the traveller no longer offers it
_wake_cm: E wakes a waystone from this far past its footprint's edge (story.rs's E reach is 2.2 m from the feet)
_arrive_cm: arriving, the player stands this far in front of the waystone, facing the way it faces: far enough that the camera, 2.6 m behind the shoulder, is clear of the waystone (at 1.6 m it was inside it)
_danger_m: no travel while a foe with its blade out is this near (the camp lookout's sight, camp.rs), or while a foe holds on the player
_traveller: metres east and south of the crossroads: west of the lane, clear of the rocks lying east of it; facing east, toward whoever comes up the lane from the village; the pack mule behind, facing the road
_dark_ticks: the view fades to dark over this long before the player is moved (the page's veil eases over 1.3 s)
_right_ticks: the played song holds on the staff this long before the waystones show
_wrong_ticks: a wrong phrase fades from the staff over this long, then the staff is clear to play again
